\section[a polémica]{a polémica — the controversy, the public row}

\label{lesson:PT-C347-polemica}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the conclusion, then the Portuguese for the criterion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a polémica}
\textbf{a polémica} — \textquotedblleft{}the controversy, the public row\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O novo horário criou uma grande polémica na escola.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The new timetable caused a big controversy at the school.}
\end{quote}

European \emph{polémica}; Brazil \emph{polêmica}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{polémica} is usually traced to French \emph{polémique} \textquotedblleft{}polemic\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB derives from Greek \emph{polemikós} \textquotedblleft{}of war\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{pólemos} \textquotedblleft{}war\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a polémica}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a polémica}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the conclusion, then the Portuguese for the criterion, then say \emph{a polémica} again
\end{itemize}

\section[contestar]{contestar — to dispute, to challenge}

\label{lesson:PT-C347-contestar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the controversy, then the Portuguese for controversial.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: contestar}
\textbf{contestar} — \textquotedblleft{}to dispute, to challenge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Os vizinhos contestaram a decisão da câmara.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The neighbours challenged the council's decision.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Contestar uma multa} — to dispute a fine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{contestar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{contestārī} \textquotedblleft{}to call to witness\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built from \emph{con-} and \emph{testārī} \textquotedblleft{}to bear witness\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{testis} \textquotedblleft{}witness\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[rebater]{rebater — to rebut, to counter; to hit back}

\label{lesson:PT-C347-rebater}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for controversial, then the Portuguese for to dispute.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: rebater}
\textbf{rebater} — \textquotedblleft{}to rebut, to counter; to hit back\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ela rebateu as críticas com calma.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She rebutted the criticism calmly.}
\end{quote}

Literally to beat back, as with a ball.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rebater} is built from \emph{re-} \textquotedblleft{}back\textquotedblright{} and \emph{bater} \textquotedblleft{}to beat\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited from Latin \emph{battuere} \textquotedblleft{}to beat, to strike\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[relevante]{relevante — relevant, important}

\label{lesson:PT-C347-relevante}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to dispute, then the Portuguese for to rebut.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: relevante}
\textbf{relevante} — \textquotedblleft{}relevant, important\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Essa informação não é relevante agora.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{That information is not relevant now.}
\end{quote}

The opposite is \emph{irrelevante}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{relevante} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{relevāns} (EtymDB), the present participle of \emph{relevāre} \textquotedblleft{}to lift up, to raise\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{levāre} \textquotedblleft{}to raise\textquotedblright{}: what is relevant stands out.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
